AFWD.justification: the directional pull that draws the fiber through the previous loop

AREV.justification: the retraction of excess material to tighten the internal diameter of a link

CLINK.justification: the mechanism that propagates the structural properties of one unit to the next in sequence

ENGAGR.justification: the state where the fiber is simultaneously pulling against itself and pushing against the boundary

EVALF.justification: the failure of the linker to maintain the required distance between units

EVALT.justification: the successful maintenance of the spatial gap required for the moat unit

FFUSE.justification: the re-integration of the dual loops back into a single structural strand

FSPLIT.justification: the point where a single strand divides to form the dual-loop structure of the hodge-link

IFIX.justification: the permanent hardening of the fiber position through heat or chemical bonding

IMSCRIB.justification: the inherent material property that remains unchanged regardless of the geometric configuration

TANCH.justification: the final constraint that prevents the unraveling of the three-unit assembly

VINIT.justification: the raw material exists prior to any topological definition or tensioning

phase_3.both_description: a transition point where a loop is both a finish for one unit and a start for the next
phase_3.false_description: a tangled or slipped loop requiring rework
phase_3.true_description: a secure and correctly spaced stitch unit
phase_3.void_description: the empty space before the first needle insertion

steps.domain_action: prepare raw fiber for the three-unit stitch
extend fiber to define the moat perimeter
broadcast the moat tension to the next segment
divide the strand to initiate the hodge-link
hold both loops of the hodge-link in simultaneous tension
retract slack to calibrate the hodge-link diameter
merge the hodge-link loops back into a single path
verify the fiber identity remains intact after the link
broadcast the hodge-link geometry to the structural linker
project the structural linker toward the terminal anchor
test the linker for load-bearing capacity
linker holds the required structural load
linker fails and requires immediate retraction
return to the start of the linker segment if failure occurs
resolve the load-bearing test into a stable segment
apply thermal set to lock the three-unit geometry
seal the terminal knot to close the system
